mainTopic: מרור (planting, fresh vs. dry, מעשר שני) and things that can or cannot become חמץ
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge from the previous amud. The ruling that all types of מרור may share one garden bed seems unnecessary, since a משנה in כלאים already allows several species in one bed. After two rejected answers, the גמרא concludes that the ruling was needed for חזרת. Because חזרת hardens like a cabbage stalk, we might have thought it needs extra space. Next, רב חסדא teaches that dry מרור is acceptable only for the stalk, while leaves must be fresh, and the גמרא defends this against the משנה's wording and a ברייתא. רמי בר חמא then asks whether מרור of מעשר שני can be used. רבא answers that מצה and מרור follow the same rule. A new משנה forbids soaking bran or chewing wheat on פסח, since they may become חמץ. The גמרא then discusses foods that cannot leaven, dripping water on flour, the dish ותיקא, and מר זוטרא's warning about coating a pot. The amud ends as רב יוסף begins a warning about scalding, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה about planting five species in one small garden bed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה in כלאים that lets five different seeds grow in one 6x6 bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A garden bed that is six by six טפחים: one may plant five kinds of seeds in it. Four go on the four sides of the bed, and one goes in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge it began on the previous amud. It quotes a משנה showing that different species may share one bed if they are spaced properly, which suggests the earlier ruling about מרור was unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ruling said all types of מרור may be planted together. But this משנה already allows different species in one bed when they are placed apart. So why did anyone need to state the ruling about מרור at all?

keyTerms.meaning: Kinds of seeds / small seed crops
The prohibition of planting mixed species together

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge (that we already learned this ruling in a משנה, so it seems unnecessary) was introduced on the previous amud. This line is the source being quoted for that question. It is not a new statement of its own.

phrases.aramaic: עֲרוּגָה שֶׁהִיא שִׁשָּׁה עַל שִׁשָּׁה טְפָחִים —
phrases.english: A garden bed that is six by six handbreadths —
one may plant in it five kinds of seeds,
four — on the four sides of the bed,
phrases.notes: Each species is placed along a different side, so they stay separate.

phrases.english: and one in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲרוּגָה שֶׁהִיא שִׁשָּׁה עַל שִׁשָּׁה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge (begun on the previous amud) against the earlier ruling about מרור and כלאים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier ruling that all types of מרור may be planted in one bed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already permits different species in one bed when properly spaced, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Maybe we would think the משנה only applies to seeds, not vegetables
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed because we might have limited the משנה to seeds and assumed vegetables are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: that applies only to seeds, but not to vegetables. So the ruling teaches us that vegetables are also permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the earlier ruling. The משנה spoke about seeds, so we might have thought vegetables like מרור are not included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer assumes vegetables could be stricter than seeds. If so, the משנה's permission would not reach them. On this reading, the ruling about מרור adds that vegetables are permitted too.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)

phrases.english: You might have said:
this applies only to seeds,
but with vegetables — no,
so it teaches us (that vegetables are also permitted).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה by limiting that משנה to seeds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the source (seeds only)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Vegetables are stricter than seeds and may not be planted together.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling teaches that vegetables are also permitted.

steps.title: But vegetables are actually more lenient than seeds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: a משנה shows vegetables are more lenient than seeds, not stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you saying vegetables are stricter than seeds? But we learned in a משנה: all kinds of seeds may not be planted in one bed, while all kinds of vegetables may be planted in one bed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 2. Another משנה says vegetables are treated more leniently than seeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 assumed vegetables might be stricter. This משנה says the reverse: seeds may not share a bed, but vegetables may. So no one would think vegetables are forbidden when seeds are allowed.

phrases.english: Is that to say that vegetables are stricter than seeds?
But didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִינֵי זְרָעִים אֵין זוֹרְעִין בַּעֲרוּגָה אַחַת,
phrases.english: all kinds of seeds — one may not plant them in one bed,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִינֵי יְרָקוֹת זוֹרְעִין בַּעֲרוּגָה אַחַת!
phrases.english: all kinds of vegetables — one may plant them in one bed!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דִּירָקוֹת אַלִּימָא מִזְּרָעִים? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that vegetables might be stricter than seeds
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה in כלאים explicitly treats vegetables more leniently than seeds.

steps.title: Maybe we would think מרור counts as a seed
steps.stepSummary: A new answer: the ruling is needed because we might have classified the מרור plants as seeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that these types of מרור are a kind of seed. So the ruling teaches us that they count as vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new defense. The ruling's point is about category: מרור counts as a vegetable, so the lenient vegetable rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since vegetables are lenient and seeds are strict, the key question is which group מרור belongs to. If מרור were a seed, it could not share a bed. The ruling would teach that it is a vegetable.

keyTerms.meaning: Bitter herbs eaten at the סדר

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא הָנֵי מָרוֹר מִין זְרָעִים נִינְהוּ,
phrases.english: You might have said these bitter herbs are a kind of seed,
so it teaches us (that they are vegetables).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא הָנֵי מָרוֹר מִין זְרָעִים נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 2 with a new reason the ruling was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the subject (which category מרור belongs to)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מרור is a type of seed and so may not share a bed.
steps.terutzMaskana: מרור is a vegetable and may be planted together.

steps.title: But every source calls מרור vegetables
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this: the משנה, בר קפרא, and the school of שמואל all call מרור 'vegetables'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could you really think they are seeds? But our משנה says 'vegetables', בר קפרא taught 'vegetables', and the school of שמואל taught 'vegetables'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 4. Three different sources already call מרור 'vegetables', so no one would mistake it for a seed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה about מרור (earlier on this daf) uses the word ירקות, and so do two ברייתות. With three sources saying it so clearly, the ruling could not have been needed just to teach that מרור is a vegetable.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (rhetorical: surely not)

phrases.english: Could you think they are seeds?
But we learned in the משנה: 'vegetables',
and בר קפרא taught: 'vegetables',
and the school of שמואל taught: 'vegetables'!

steps.triggerLanguage: זְרָעִים סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that one might classify מרור as seeds
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three sources already explicitly call מרור 'vegetables'.

steps.title: The ruling was needed for lettuce, which hardens
steps.stepSummary: The final answer: the ruling was needed for חזרת. Since it eventually hardens, we might have thought it needs extra space.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed for חזרת (lettuce). You might have thought: since it eventually hardens, we should give it more space.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final reason for the ruling. It focuses on one specific type of מרור, חזרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזרת starts soft, but its stalk later becomes hard and woody. Because of that, one might think it needs a wider gap from other plants than ordinary vegetables do. The ruling teaches that it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Lettuce, the first type of מרור listed
He needed it (the ruling was necessary)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether חזרת is a vegetable; it clearly is. The question is only how much space it needs. This is a matter of how the rule is carried out, not of which category חזרת belongs to.

phrases.english: It was necessary for him regarding lettuce.
It could have entered your mind to say:
since it will eventually harden —
let us give it more space.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲזֶרֶת אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 4 with a narrower reason focused on חזרת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the ruling to a specific case (חזרת)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because חזרת hardens, it needs extra space from other plants.
steps.terutzMaskana: חזרת may be planted with the other types of מרור without extra space.

steps.title: Support for the mistaken idea from the hardened cabbage stalk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows why the mistaken idea was reasonable: a hardened cabbage stalk does get extra space. The ruling teaches that חזרת does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא say that a cabbage stalk that has hardened is given a בית רובע of space? This shows that once something will harden, we give it more space. So here too, we might give חזרת more space. The ruling teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show that the idea in Step 6 was a real possibility. It then closes the discussion: the ruling teaches that חזרת does not get extra space.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hardened cabbage stalk needs a large empty area around it, called a בית רובע. Comparing חזרת to cabbage makes the mistaken idea believable. The final 'קא משמע לן' tells us חזרת is treated like the other soft vegetables, not like cabbage.

keyTerms.meaning: An area large enough to sow a quarter קב of seed
This shows that... (a conclusion drawn from a source)

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling that all types of מרור may share one bed was needed only for חזרת. Even though חזרת hardens like cabbage, it does not need extra space from the other types of מרור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the classic 'מהו דתימא' pattern. The גמרא keeps searching for the most believable mistake a ruling could prevent. It rejects weak options until it finds one with a real basis, here the cabbage comparison.

phrases.aramaic: לָאו אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina say:
a cabbage stalk that has hardened —
we widen for it a בית רובע of space!
This shows: since it will eventually harden,
we give it more space;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי נִיתֵּיב לַהּ רַוְוחָא טְפֵי,
phrases.english: here too, let us give it (lettuce) more space —
so it teaches us (that lettuce needs no extra space).
phrases.notes: This wraps up the discussion: the point of the ruling is that חזרת shouldn't be compared to cabbage.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the mistaken idea of Step 6 with a parallel case, then concludes that the ruling teaches otherwise.
steps.raayaObject: That one might reasonably think חזרת needs extra space
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: a hardened cabbage stalk is given a בית רובע
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: חזרת does not need extra space. All types of מרור may be planted together in one bed.

steps.title: רב חסדא limits 'fresh or dry' to the stalk
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the משנה's permission to use dry מרור applies only to the stalk. Leaves must be fresh.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one fulfills the מצוה with them whether fresh or dry. רב חסדא said: this was taught only about the stalk. But the leaves count only when fresh, not when dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה, and רב חסדא explains that it has a limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to allow dry מרור without any condition. רב חסדא narrows this. A dry stalk is acceptable, but dry leaves are not, because they no longer count as proper מרור.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about... (a limiting formula)

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא does not disagree with the משנה. He explains which part of the plant the משנה is talking about.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹצְאִין בָּהֶן בֵּין לַחִין בֵּין יְבֵשִׁין כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: One fulfills the obligation with them, whether fresh or dry, etc.
Rav Chisda said:
They taught this only about the stalk,
but regarding the leaves,
fresh ones, yes; dry ones, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בַּקֶּלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic in the משנה: fresh versus dry מרור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dry מרור is acceptable only for the stalk. Leaves must be fresh.

steps.title: The משנה's wording suggests the first clause is about leaves
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentions 'their stalk' separately at the end. That implies the earlier clause, including 'fresh or dry', refers to leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the end of the משנה says 'with their stalk', doesn't that show that the beginning of the משנה is about leaves?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from the order of the words in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה lists the stalk separately later, then the earlier 'fresh or dry' seems to describe the leaves. That would mean dry leaves are acceptable, which contradicts רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of a משנה
The first clause of a משנה

phrases.english: But since the last clause teaches
'with their stalk',
it follows that the first clause is about leaves?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's limit.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that 'fresh or dry' applies only to the stalk
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mentioning the stalk later implies the earlier clause refers to leaves, so dry leaves would be acceptable.

steps.title: The משנה's later words explain the earlier clause
steps.stepSummary: The mention of 'their stalk' does not add a new item. It explains that 'fresh or dry' was about the stalk.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is explaining itself: when it said 'whether fresh or dry', it meant the stalk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא by reading the end of the משנה as an explanation, not a new item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'with their stalk' clarifies the earlier words instead of adding something new. So 'fresh or dry' refers to the stalk, which is exactly what רב חסדא said.

phrases.english: It is explaining:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָתָנֵי בֵּין לַחִין בֵּין יְבֵשִׁין —
phrases.english: when it teaches 'whether fresh or dry' —
that is about the stalk.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרוֹשֵׁי קָא מְפָרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: the later phrase explains rather than adds
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'With their stalk' is a separate item, so the first clause is about leaves.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'With their stalk' explains that 'fresh or dry' refers to the stalk.

steps.title: A ברייתא has רבי מאיר allowing even dry herbs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי מאיר allowing the herbs and their stalks, fresh or dry. The חכמים allow only fresh ones. The ברייתא ends with a general rule based on the taste of מרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: one fulfills the מצוה with the herbs and with their stalk, whether fresh or dry. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: fresh ones are acceptable, dry ones are not. Everyone agrees that wilted ones are acceptable, but not pickled, overcooked, or cooked. The general rule: anything that still has the taste of מרור is acceptable, and anything without the taste of מרור is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב חסדא again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי מאיר lists 'the herbs' (the leaves) and 'their stalk' together, and then says 'fresh or dry'. That sounds like dry leaves are also acceptable, which goes against רב חסדא's limit on our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Wilted, no longer fresh but not fully dry

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up כמושין (wilted, acceptable here) with יבשין (fully dry, which the חכמים reject).

phrases.english: They challenged:
One fulfills the obligation with them and with their stalk,
whether fresh or dry,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
fresh ones, one fulfills the obligation with them;
dry ones, one does not fulfill the obligation with them.
And all agree that one fulfills the obligation with them when wilted.
But not pickled ones,
and not overcooked ones, and not cooked ones.
The general rule is:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ טַעַם מָרוֹר — יוֹצְאִין בּוֹ,
phrases.english: anything that has the taste of maror, one fulfills the obligation with it;

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ טַעַם מָרוֹר — אֵין יוֹצְאִין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: and anything that lacks the taste of maror, one does not fulfill the obligation with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה's wording was resolved, a ברייתא is brought against רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that dry leaves are not acceptable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר says 'fresh or dry' about both the herbs and the stalk, which suggests dry leaves are acceptable.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's 'fresh or dry' refers to the stalk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads רבי מאיר's 'fresh or dry' as referring only to the stalk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Explain it as referring to the stalk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the ברייתא the same way it answered the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Fresh or dry' in the ברייתא applies only to the stalk, not to the leaves. So רבי מאיר also agrees that leaves must be fresh, and רב חסדא's rule stands.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא, a dry stalk of מרור is acceptable, but leaves must be fresh. The משנה and the ברייתא are both read so that 'fresh or dry' refers to the stalk.

phrases.english: Interpret it as referring to the stalk.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגּוּמָא אַקֶּלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a phrase
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר allows dry leaves as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר's 'fresh or dry' refers only to the stalk.

steps.title: A dispute over wilted מרור
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says wilted מרור is not acceptable. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says it is acceptable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: one does not fulfill the מצוה with them when wilted. In the name of רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק they said: one does fulfill the מצוה with them when wilted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a מחלוקת about wilted מרור. The topic then ends: the next step moves on to an unrelated question from רמי בר חמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא said that everyone agrees wilted מרור is acceptable (ושוין). This ברייתא brings a first, unnamed opinion that wilted מרור is not acceptable, while רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says it is. The גמרא quotes this ברייתא without comment and moves on to רמי בר חמא's question.
steps.confusionAlert: This seems to clash with 'ושוין שיוצאין בהן כמושין' in the previous ברייתא. The גמרא does not take this up here. The next step turns to a different topic.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One does not fulfill the obligation with them when wilted.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אָמְרוּ:
phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok they said:
One fulfills the obligation with them when wilted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין יוֹצְאִין בָּהֶן כְּמוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source about wilted מרור, which seems to conflict with the 'all agree' line in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion rejects wilted מרור. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק accepts it.

steps.title: Can מרור of מעשר שני be used?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks whether one can fulfill the מרור obligation with מעשר שני produce in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: Can a person fulfill his obligation with מרור that is מעשר שני, eaten in ירושלים?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא opens a new question. Can a person use מרור that is מעשר שני to fulfill the מצוה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא discussed whether מצה made from מעשר שני works for the מצוה. רבי עקיבא says yes and רבי יוסי הגלילי says no. Now רמי בר חמא asks the same question about מרור.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked / raised a question (a real open question)
Second tithe, produce that must be eaten in ירושלים

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama asked:
What is the law, can a person fulfill his obligation
with bitter herbs of second tithe in Jerusalem?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of wilted מרור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether מעשר שני produce can be used for the מרור obligation.

steps.title: According to רבי עקיבא there is no question
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי עקיבא allows מעשר שני for the Torah מצוה of מצה, it surely works for the rabbinic מרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי עקיבא, you have no question. If one fulfills the Torah-level obligation of מצה with it, is it even a question for the rabbinic obligation of מרור?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the question. It shows that according to רבי עקיבא, the answer is obviously yes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a קל וחומר. Today, with no קרבן פסח, מצה is a Torah obligation and מרור is only rabbinic. If רבי עקיבא allows מעשר שני for the stricter Torah מצוה, he would surely allow it for the lighter rabbinic one.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, if even (opens a קל וחומר)

steps.confusionAlert: מרור is rabbinic here only because there is no קרבן פסח nowadays. When the קרבן פסח is brought, eating מרור is from the Torah.

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ:
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Akiva, do not ask it:
now, if with matza, a Torah obligation, one fulfills it,
is it a question with bitter herbs, a rabbinic obligation?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the question in step 14 by removing רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי עקיבא, yes, by קל וחומר from מצה.

steps.title: The real question: according to רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי forbids מעשר שני for מצה. Does that apply to rabbinic מרור, or do rabbinic rules copy Torah rules?
steps.simpleTranslation: Where you should ask is according to רבי יוסי הגלילי. What is the law? Is it only with Torah-level מצה that one does not fulfill the obligation, but with rabbinic מרור one does? Or perhaps whatever the Rabbis instituted, they made it like Torah law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the real question, which is according to רבי יוסי הגלילי. It lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: רבי יוסי הגלילי's ban is only for the Torah מצוה of מצה, so rabbinic מרור could be more lenient. Side two: when the Rabbis make a מצוה, they model it on the Torah version. If so, מרור would follow the same ban as מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Where you should ask the question

keyTerms.term: כׇּל דְּתַקִּינוּ רַבָּנַן כְּעֵין דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא תַּקּוּן
keyTerms.meaning: Whatever the Rabbis instituted, they made it like Torah law

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle כל דתקינו רבנן כעין דאורייתא תקון shows up across ש״ס. It means rabbinic laws often copy the structure of the Torah laws they are based on.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, מַאי?
phrases.english: Where you should ask is according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili: what is the law?
Is it only with matza, a Torah obligation, that one does not fulfill it,
but with bitter herbs, a rabbinic obligation, one does fulfill it?
Or perhaps: whatever the Rabbis instituted,
they instituted it like Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting רבי עקיבא aside, it shows where the question really applies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, is rabbinic מרור more lenient than Torah מצה, or does it follow the Torah model?

steps.title: רבא: מצה and מרור are treated the same
steps.stepSummary: רבא says it is logical that מצה and מרור share the same rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It makes sense that מצה and מרור are alike.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. מרור follows the same rule as מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links them: "על מצות ומררים יאכלהו". So the Rabbis' מרור keeps the Torah's pairing with מצה. According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, מעשר שני does not work for מרור, just as it does not work for מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Matza and bitter herbs, linked together in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, מרור of מעשר שני works. According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, רבא rules that it does not, because מצה and מרור go together.

phrases.english: Rava said: It stands to reason that matza and bitter herbs are alike.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מַצָּה וּמָרוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the question raised in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מרור follows מצה, so according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, מעשר שני is not valid for מרור.

steps.title: New משנה: soaking bran and chewing wheat on פסח
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids soaking bran for chickens or for washing, and forbids chewing wheat to place on a wound, because these may become חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not soak bran for chickens, but one may pour boiling water on it. A woman may not soak bran to carry in her hand to the bathhouse, but she may rub it dry on her skin. A person may not chew wheat and put it on his wound, because it becomes חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists ways grain or bran could become חמץ on פסח through contact with water or saliva.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soaking lets bran sit in water and turn into חמץ. Pouring boiling water on it is allowed because the scalding is quick and stops leavening. Rubbing dry bran on the skin is allowed, but chewed wheat becomes חמץ from saliva.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may not soak coarse bran for chickens,
but one may scald it with boiling water.
A woman may not soak coarse bran
to carry in her hand to the bathhouse,
but she may rub it on her skin dry.
A person may not chew wheat
and place it on his wound,
because it becomes leavened.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין שׁוֹרִין אֶת הַמּוּרְסָן לְתַרְנְגוֹלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the מרור discussion and opens a new משנה about things that may become חמץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Soaking bran and chewing wheat are forbidden on פסח because they become חמץ. Scalding bran and rubbing dry bran on the skin are permitted.

steps.title: Foods that cannot become חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא: baked food, cooked food, and dough scalded in boiling water cannot become חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The חכמים taught: These are things that cannot become חמץ: something baked, something cooked, and dough that was scalded in boiling water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא lists three kinds of food that can no longer turn into חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once dough has been fully baked, or has been put into boiling water, the heat stops the leavening process. So after that point, water cannot make it rise. The next step will challenge the item 'cooked'.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that comes after the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא on this משנה

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין בָּאִין לִידֵי חִימּוּץ:
phrases.english: These are things that do not come to a state of leavening:
the baked, and the cooked,
and scalded dough that one scalded in boiling water.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין בָּאִין לִידֵי חִימּוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה about things that may come to חמץ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Baked food, cooked food, and dough scalded in boiling water cannot become חמץ.

steps.title: How can cooked dough not become חמץ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the word 'cooked': while raw dough is slowly cooking, it will already become חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cooked? By the time it gets cooked, it has already become חמץ!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges one item on the list. Raw dough put into water to cook would have time to leaven before the cooking finishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is timing. Cooking raw dough is slow, so the dough sits in water and can rise before the heat stops it. So how can the ברייתא say cooked food is safe?

keyTerms.meaning: By the time it gets cooked

phrases.english: Cooked?
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא in order to question it

phrases.english: By the time it is cooked, it becomes leavened!

steps.triggerLanguage: מְבוּשָּׁל? אַדִּמְבַשֵּׁל לֵיהּ, מַחְמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one item in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that cooked food cannot become חמץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Raw dough leavens during the slow cooking process, before the heat can stop it.

steps.title: רב פפא: it means baked and then cooked
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the ברייתא means food that was first baked and only then cooked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The ברייתא is talking about something baked that was afterward cooked.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by reading 'cooked' in a narrow way. It means dough that was already baked before it was cooked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the baking already stopped the leavening, cooking it afterward in water cannot make it חמץ. Raw dough that goes straight into the pot is not included, and it can still become חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Baked food that was then cooked
'He is saying.' This explains what a text really means

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the ברייתא as permitting all cooked dough. Raw dough boiled in water can still become חמץ. Only dough that was already baked is safe.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It means baked food that one then cooked.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הָאָפוּי שֶׁבִּישְּׁלוֹ קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by reinterpreting a word in the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of a term in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Cooked' includes raw dough boiled in water.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Cooked' means already-baked food that was then cooked, so it cannot leaven.

steps.title: Flour under dripping water does not leaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה rules that flour with water dripping into it all day does not become חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: Flour that water is dripping into, even for the whole day, does not become חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about flour that has water leaking onto it. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says it does not become חמץ, even after a full day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dough leavens when it is left to sit still. Water that keeps landing on the flour keeps it moving, so it never gets the rest it needs to rise. The next step will add a condition to this rule.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
Flour into which dripping water fell,
even for the entire day,
does not come to a state of leavening.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling on the same theme of when flour and water do not become חמץ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flour under dripping water does not become חמץ, even after a whole day.

steps.title: רב פפא: only when the dripping is nonstop
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא limits the rule to a case where the drops fall one right after another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is only when one drop falls right after the other drop.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a condition to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's rule. The dripping must be continuous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flour stays safe only because it never gets a still moment. If there are pauses between drops, the wet flour can sit and leaven. So slow dripping with gaps does become חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And that is only when.' This adds a limiting condition
Drop right after drop, nonstop dripping

steps.whatToRemember: Constant dripping prevents leavening because the flour never rests. Gaps between drops let it become חמץ.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
And that is when it drips drop after drop.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: וְהוּא דְּעָבֵיד טִיף לַהֲדֵי טִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limiting condition to the previous ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dripping-flour rule applies only when the drops are continuous.

steps.title: The school of רבי שילא permits ותיקא
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי שילא rules that ותיקא, a flour-based dish mixed with liquids, is permitted on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי שילא say: ותיקא is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling that a dish called ותיקא may be eaten on פסח. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ותיקא is a dish made by mixing flour with liquids. The school of רבי שילא holds it does not become חמץ. A contradicting source is about to be quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study hall) of רבי שילא
A dish of flour mixed with liquids

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Sheila say:
Vatika is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי שֵׁילָא: וָתִיקָא שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling on another flour-and-liquid food

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids ותיקא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling with a ברייתא that says ותיקא is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches that ותיקא is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the school of רבי שילא with a ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One source permits ותיקא and another forbids it. The two seem to contradict each other directly.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught that vatika is forbidden?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא וָתִיקָא אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the previous ruling from a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The school of רבי שילא's permission of ותיקא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly rules that ותיקא is forbidden.

steps.title: Oil and salt versus water and salt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: ותיקא made with oil and salt is permitted, and ותיקא made with water and salt is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. This source is about ותיקא made with oil and salt, and that source is about ותיקא made with water and salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sources are describing different recipes, so they do not really argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil is not water, so it does not cause leavening, and the oil-and-salt version is permitted. With water, the dough can become חמץ, so the water-and-salt version is forbidden. The deciding factor is whether water is used.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult.' This introduces an answer

steps.whatToRemember: ותיקא with oil and salt is permitted. ותיקא with water and salt is forbidden, because water causes חמץ.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is where one made it with oil and salt,
that is where one made it with water and salt.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּעַבְדֵיהּ בְּמִישְׁחָא וּמִילְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction by splitting the cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources argue about the same dish.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permitting source means oil and salt, and the forbidding source means water and salt.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: do not coat a pot with roasted flour
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא warns against coating a pot with roasted-grain flour, because some may not be fully roasted and could become חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: A person should not coat a pot with roasted-grain flour, because it may not be properly roasted, and it will become חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא gives a practical warning about a kitchen habit on פסח: coating a pot with flour made from roasted grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Roasted grain is normally safe from leavening, because the heat already acted on it. But some kernels may not have been roasted well enough. Those could leaven when they get wet in the pot.

keyTerms.meaning: To coat or line a pot

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
A person should not coat a pot
with flour of roasted grain,
lest it was not properly roasted,
and it will come to a state of leavening.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: לָא לִימַחֵי אִינִישׁ קִדְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new practical warning in the same series of rules about flour and liquid
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not coat a pot with roasted-grain flour, in case some was not fully roasted and becomes חמץ.

steps.title: רב יוסף begins a warning about scalding
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף begins a similar warning against scalding something. The statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: A person should not scald...
steps.whatsHappening: This line only opens רב יוסף's statement. The rest of his warning comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like מר זוטרא, רב יוסף is about to warn against a kitchen practice that could lead to חמץ. It involves scalding, the same method mentioned in the ברייתא at the start.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
A person should not scald
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לָא לִיחְלוֹט אִינִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a parallel practical warning, following מר זוטרא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Incomplete here: רב יוסף warns against a certain kind of scalding (completed on the next amud).
